title: Why is MV's fullscreen blurry but in 2003 it's not?

posts.author: HolyChaos
posts.body: I don't get why the newer and advanced engines can't have fullscreen without the game looking ugly while in 2003 (And I assume the same is for 2000 as well) going fullscreen retains the quality of the graphics. I'd make a game in 2003 if it wasn't so limited compared to MV purely because of this, not being able to play a game in fullscreen is a nightmare.

posts.author: Spacialrended
posts.body:
Oh I 100% agree with you. It's a problem i've seen with both VX Ace and MV and it really bums me out because its easier for my attention deficit brain to focus on the game when It's in full screen.
I'm sure there's a script for that! ... Somewhere!

posts.author: DevRPG2k
posts.body:
RM2k/2k3 uses DirectX, and after the update, 2k3 uses GDI.
When using DirectX, fullscreen is the "Exclusive" mode, meaning it changes the player's monitor resolution to 320x240, even if the player's monitor settings don't have this option.
RMMV and MZ, on the other hand, use WebGL or Canvas, meaning it's basically an HTML page with a browser game running inside it. Therefore, for the pixels to work perfectly, the scaling must be correct (mathematical).
RM2k3, which uses GDI in fullscreen mode, is not "Exclusive," so depending on the monitor's scaling and with smoothing turned off, the pixels will also be distorted and it gets worse if you disable stretched mode.
